newsitem.title: INDIA: Court orders factories closed to save Taj Mahal.
newsitem.headline: Court orders factories closed to save Taj Mahal.

text.p: India's Supreme Court, cracking down on chemical and carbon fumes threatening the Taj Mahal, on Monday ordered 292 coal-based industries in its vicinity to close by the end of 1997, the United News of India (UNI) said.

It said the court set December 31, 1997, as the deadline for coke or coal-based industries to get out of the Taj Trapezium, the area within a 70-km (44-mile) radius of the famed mausoleum at Agra, some 200 km (120 miles) south of New Delhi.

The court, delivering a judgement in a public interest case, also ordered officials to cut off coke and coal supplies to the industries in the area around the shining marble monument by April 30, UNI said.

"This is an unconditional order which cannot be varied. The district magistrate and police superintendent shall close all such industries after December 31, 1997," the news agency quoted judges Kuldip Singh and Faizan-uddin as saying.

Environmentalists say the monument, which attracts some 1.5 million tourists every year, half of them foreigners, has already been severely damaged by carbon smoke and sulphur dioxide fumes that cause "marble cancer," a decaying of the rock.
Last year, the Indian government announced a plan to protect the monument that included the planting of 100,000 trees and use of cleaner fuel in the Taj Trapezium.
The 17th-century monument was built by Moghul Emperor Shahjehan for his much-loved second wife, Mumtaz Mahal, along the banks of the Yamuna River.
In the past, environmentalists and authorities have faced stiff resistance from hundreds of factories in their efforts to re-locate polluting industries from the area around Agra.
The factories, including iron foundries and leather goods facilities, employ thousands of workers.
Environmentalists say pollution in the area is ten times the acceptable level.
A state-owned oil refinery in neighbouring Mathura city, regarded by environmentalists as a major threat to the Taj Mahal, was spared closure after it said it installed anti-pollution safeguards.
